note: Pinned reference media sources for native and isolated browser libzci builds. Ordinary izci frontend/server assets are independent.

toolchain.policy: Use an installed real Rust release and the committed lockfile. Windows native R2/R3 and browser R4 builds use the recorded toolchains; GNU/Linux recovery remains unverified.

browser.assembly: Separate shared Rust control/ordinary codecs, import-free audio WASM and pinned reference C codec modules; optional WebCodecs Opus uses shared Rust Ogg/timeline policy.

libraries.role: Tracker-module provider (MOD/XM/S3M/IT/MO3 surface): handle ownership, float decode, seek/subsong, finite EOF, metadata, interpolation/render controls, interactive channel mutes; probe without audio output.

The old static wrapper and its users stay untouched.

defaultExperiment.design: Rust WASM core plus separate Emscripten codec modules; native links compiled libraries directly (scaffolding Â§3).
defaultExperiment.fallback: If the synchronous-C-callback bridge (bounded FileReaderSync Blob-slice reads in a dedicated decode worker) fails, use the core's shared Ogg reader with packet-level libopus, confined to the Opus provider. Compare a unified Emscripten build on the same scenarios and document the replacement before proceeding.

firstExperiment.success: The same Opus fixture opens, decodes finite nonempty PCM, seeks on the normalized timeline, and closes through the core session/provider API on both native and browser. Native execution uses compiled media code directly with no JS/WASM runtime, webview, or Node dependency.

constraints: Only ignored output locations; preserve frontend/server assets, profiles and grants.
libzci-codecs defaults to reference Opus; the M1 CLI and native crude include modules by default. The CLI can omit modules with --no-default-features.
Windows media archives use .lib and /MD; GNU/Linux uses .a plus the appropriate native C++ runtime for optional modules.
